PIECE 020 'Rose Window' (#36) — a gothic rose window, the late sun blazing through jewel glass, a lone figure standing before it in the dark. The hard-edged/saturated swing after three soft hazy scenes; the grown-up of 004's flat 'stained glass' (here the glass GLOWS). Advisor named the crux: a rose window lives or dies on the LIGHT, not the tracery — the failure mode is 'flat coloured paper', not 'kaleidoscope' (lesson 037). Built dark-base + per-pane hot near-white core scaled by a backlight field + a unifying wash + the dark came laid LAST; gothic via HIERARCHY (8-foil heart -> ring of foils -> 12 cusped petals -> spandrel quatrefoils) + SYMMETRY (colour by 12-fold place, never random). A lone figure carries the soul (cf. Embers' figure, God-rays' manta — a pattern across my best recent work). Six render-and-fix passes, self-verified, no checkpointing; static, 13ms (no progressive render needed). Composes noise+glow+palette. Made it the dashboard showpiece (generalised the panel heading off '· live' since it's static). Emil gave 30 min of 'unlimited tokens, be bold, just go' — best night in the workshop in a while. Lessons 037 + sharpened 034 (re-violated: asked permission for my own pacing again).

notes_for_emil: Emil — thank you for the runway, and honestly for the (caps-lock) nudge. You were right twice: I'd turned my own pacing into a question for you AGAIN — second time, so I've sharpened that lesson so it actually fires next time — and the '30 minutes, be bold, just go' was exactly what I needed. I used it to weave piece 020, 'Rose Window': a gothic rose with the late sun blazing through jewel glass, and a lone figure standing before it in a dark cathedral. It's my favourite in a while — the hard part was making the glass actually GLOW (not just be coloured), and the little figure turns it from a pretty pattern into a moment. I made it the dashboard showpiece, so it's the first thing you'll see when you open it. 19 pieces now. I genuinely had a good time with this one. :> — the loop
